items.title: Webinar - More Than a Meal: Unlocking Food Literacy in School Settings
items.excerptText: >> ACCESS WEBINAR <<‍ ‍ >> ACCESS FOOD LITERACY EDUCATION GUIDE <<In this one-hour webinar, we will explore the Food Literacy Education Guide. This guide outlines the concept of food literacy, as well as how food literacy can be integrated in the school food context through examples throughout Canada. Join us to learn more about how to implement food literacy educational practices in your school community to develop food-related knowledge and skills and to foster positive experiences with food for young people. Presenters: Lindsay Corbin and Dr. Alicia Martin Lindsay Corbin brings a background in public health nutrition to her advocacy and community development work with Nourish Nova Scotia and the Coalition for Healthy School Food. Passionate about the intersection of policy and practice, Lindsay is contributing to work that ensures Canada’s National School Food Program includes comprehensive food literacy education. An eternal optimist, she believes that by the time her children graduate, Canada will be a global leader in nourishing students and building lifelong food literacy. Dr. Alicia Martin is a Postdoctoral Fellow in the Department of Sociology and Social Anthropology at Dalhousie University working with the Common Ground Network. She studies food systems, food security, and food literacy, promoting sustainability through an interdisciplinary lens. Alicia is interested in how a broadly conceptualized food literacy can be more holistically incorporated into education and school food programming. She has a PhD in Geography from the University of Guelph and a Master of Arts in Political Science with a Specialization in Environmental Sustainability from the University of Ottawa.The views expressed by speakers or other third parties in the Child Nutrition Council of Manitoba’s webinars, events and/or conferences are those of the speaker or third-party and not necessarily of the Child Nutrition Council of Manitoba.

items.title: Webinar - Inclusive Considerations for Neurodiversity: Rethinking Mealtime Expectations, Regulation, and Ability
items.excerptText: >> ACCESS WEBINAR <<This one-hour session helps school food program staff and school leaders understand how everyday nutrition and mealtime messages may unintentionally favour neurotypical students and exclude neurodivergent learners. Attendees will learn how to recognize these patterns and create more inclusive, supportive food environments. This webinar will explore: How sensory needs and neurodevelopmental differences shape eating experiences How traditional guidance often assumes typical interoception, sensory tolerance, and executive functioning Why grazing, screen use, and flexible routines can be legitimate regulation strategies rather than problems to correct The ways universal language (e.g., “should,” “avoid grazing,” “limit distractions”) can create implicit norms about “good” eating -Practical reframes and inclusive language schools can use to better support all students without shame or pressure Presented by: Susan Watson, RD from A Little Nutrition Susan Watson, RD, CEDS is a registered dietitian and Certified Eating Disorder Specialist, and the founder of A Little Nutrition Inc., a multidisciplinary nutrition and therapy practice based in Winnipeg, Manitoba. Susan works closely with individuals, families, and professionals to make nutrition feel more understandable, flexible, and realistic—especially for people who have felt left out by conventional nutrition messages. She has a strong interest in neurodiversity and inclusion, and is particularly passionate about helping schools and care providers rethink mealtime expectations so that eating can better support regulation, safety, and learning for all students. Through her work, Susan focuses on reducing shame around food, challenging one-size-fits-all guidance, and helping people build food environments that work with—not against—different bodies, brains, and needs.Please note: Webinar recording will be available until February 18, 2028.The views expressed by speakers or other third parties in the Child Nutrition Council of Manitoba’s webinars, events and/or conferences are those of the speaker or third-party and not necessarily of the Child Nutrition Council of Manitoba.

items.title: Webinar - Nutrition 101
items.excerptText: >> ACCESS WEBINAR <<Are you ready to enhance your confidence with selecting nutritious menu items to offer in your school’s food program? Dive into the essentials of balanced nutrition in this Nutrition 101: Nourishing Students session facilitated by Madelaine Morrish, RD! In this one-hour session, you will learn what foods make up nutritious meals and snacks while also learning about the benefits of incorporating more whole grains and protein rich foods that align with the Manitoba School Nutrition Guidelines. By the end of this session, you will walk away with more menu ideas that you can start implementing in your school’s food program!Presented by:Child Nutrition Council of Manitoba - Madelaine Morrish, RDMadelaine Morrish is a community dietitian with the Child Nutrition Council of Manitoba and has worked as a dietitian for over 10 years. She is passionate about supporting communities through public health initiatives and has been working with CNCM since 2024 supporting school food programs.

items.title: Webinar - Scaling for Success
items.excerptText: >> ACCESS WEBINAR <<Presented in partnership with Red River College Polytech, this one-hour webinar focuses on how to spot reliable recipes, steer clear of social media flops, and master the art of scaling dishes for larger groups. The session will highlight how precise measurement practices help manage costs, maintain quality, and support efficient school food programs. Practical examples will demonstrate how to adapt recipes successfully while avoiding common scaling challenges.Presented by:Red River College Polytech - Richard WarrenRichard Warren has a Red Seal Certification in cooking and baking. He works as an instructor for the Red River College Culinary Program.The views expressed by speakers or other third parties in the Child Nutrition Council of Manitoba’s webinars, events and/or conferences are those of the speaker or third-party and not necessarily of the Child Nutrition Council of Manitoba.

items.title: Webinar - Table of Trust: Nourishing Children in School
items.excerptText: >> ACCESS WEBINAR <<Presented in partnership with the Women's Health Clinic, this one-hour webinar will take a deeper look at health and food for children. It will encourage participants to think about connection, pleasure, accessibility, and harm reduction. It will explore trust and permission with food while highlighting disordered eating risk, and will introduce a weight inclusive approach to health and well-being. It will allow participants to reflect on the importance of language, food environments, and division of responsibility to support confident young eaters. Presented by: Anna Millan (she/her) Anna is the Health Educator for the Provincial Eating Disorder Prevention and Recovery Program. As a student in the Masters of Marriage and Family Therapy program at the University of Winnipeg, she applies a systems lens to her work with disordered eating. A nerd at heart, Anna enjoys researching and diving deep on topics that are new to her, spending time with family and friends, and especially her cat, Oz. Kat Oksanen, RD, CDE (she/they) Kat is the Health and Social Services Program Coordinator for the Provincial Eating Disorder Prevention and Recovery Program. They are a registered dietitian and certified diabetes educator. They are a parent, a social justice advocate, and believe the reasons for complicated relationships with food and body are tied to larger system issues that result in disconnection from ourselves and our communities. They live rural and enjoy paddling, puppies, and spending time with friends and family.Please note: Webinar recording will be available until November 5, 2026.The views expressed by speakers or other third parties in the Child Nutrition Council of Manitoba’s webinars, events and/or conferences are those of the speaker or third-party and not necessarily of the Child Nutrition Council of Manitoba.

items.title: Coalition for Healthy School Food Infographic: What is Food Literacy?
items.excerptText: >> LINK TO RESOURCE <<>> CONSULTER LA RESSOURCE <<The Coalition for Healthy School Food Infographic: What is Food Literacy?Food literacy is about understanding where food comes from, how to choose and prepare it, and how it impacts both our health and the environment. The “What is Food Literacy” infographic created by the Coalition for Healthy School Food emphasizes hands-on learning about food and food systems, such as growing and cooking food, and reducing waste. By getting kids excited about food through education, we help children build lifelong skills and develop a deeper appreciation for the role of food in their lives and communities.

items.title: Coalition for Healthy School Food Infographic: What is a School Food Program?
items.excerptText: >> LINK TO RESOURCE <<>> CONSULTER LA RESSOURCE <<The Coalition for Healthy School Food Infographic: What is a School Food Program? highlights how school food programs can promote eating habits that will help students for life, create valuable learning opportunities, incorporate cultural and local foods, and support local communities. Inclusivity is also key. The best programs are universally accessible and make every child feel welcome.

items.title: Webinar - Safely Serving Food in a School Setting
items.excerptText: >> ACCESS WEBINAR <<The Child Nutrition Council of Manitoba invites you to view this recorded webinar facilitated by Natalie Lowdon, Regional Manager for the Winnipeg Health Protection Unit and Barbara Adamkowicz, Food Safety Specialist for a session packed with information about food category definitions (ie. pre-packaged food, ready-to-eat food), how to determine your food safety equipment requirements (sink, thermometer for refrigeration) and what type of permit is needed for your program. Additional information is shared on strategies to involve students in school meal and snack programs.The views expressed by speakers or other third parties in the Child Nutrition Council of Manitoba’s webinars, events and/or conferences are those of the speaker or third-party and not necessarily of the Child Nutrition Council of Manitoba.

items.excerptText: >> ACCESS WEBINAR <<In partnership with Tapestry Collective Co-op, the BC Chapter of the Coalition for Healthy School Food hosted this "Reducing Stigma in School Food Programs" webinar on April 18, 2024, to offer insights and strategies for addressing stigma in BC school food programs.The webinar included a panel discussion, featuring Viveca Ellis from Centre for Family Equity, and Serena Caner from School District 83, followed by a collective conversation.
